1940.subject: Zoology
1940.text: An artificial pacemaker is implanted subcutaneously and connected to the heart in patients
options: having 90 % blockage of the three main coronary arteries
having a very high blood pressure
with irregularity in the heart rhythm
1940.sol: Artificial pacemaker is a medical device designed to regulate the beating of the heart. The purpose of an artificial pacemaker is to stimulate the heart when either the heart's native pacemaker is not fast enough or if there are blocks in the heart's electrical conducting system preventing the propagation of electrical impulses from the native pacemaker to the lower chambers of the heart, known as the ventricles. Generally, pacemakers do not treat fast rhythms of the heart.

1962.sol: WBCs can change their shape like Amoeba and are thus, capable of amoeboid movement. This enables them to squeeze out of blood capillaries into the tissues. This process is called diapedesis.

2016.subject: Zoology

2016.sol: Thyroxine, the principal hormone, of thyroid gland, is required for tissue differentiation and metamorphosis (the rapid transformation from the larval to the adult form) in amphibians. Thyroxine triggers a response from the hypothalamus, (probably by a genetic mechanism) followed by the production and release of TSH (Thyroid stimulating hormone), thus metamorphosis begins and tadpoles metamorphose into frogs. 2054.subject: Zoology
2054.text: The renal fluid isotonic to the cortical fluid and blood is found in
options: distal convoluted tubule and ascending limb
the proximal convoluted tubule and distal convoluted tubule
the ascending limb and descending limb.
2054.sol: The renal fluid filtrate is isotonic to blood plasma in proximal convoluted tubule and distal convoluted tubule. The filtrate is hypertonic to blood plasma in descending limb of loop of Henle and hypotonic to blood plasma in ascending limb of loop of Henle. Renal fluid is hypertonic to blood plasma and isotonic to medullary fluid in collecting duct.

63491.subject: Mathematics
63491.text: The number of ways that 8 beads of different colours can be strung to form a necklace is
63491.sol: The number of ways to arrange n distinct objects in a circle is (n-1)! . For a necklace, clockwise and counter-clockwise arrangements are considered identical because it can be flipped over. Therefore, the number of ways to string n different beads into a necklace is (n-1)! 2 . Given n = 8 , the number of ways is (8-1)! 2 = 7! 2 . Since 7! = 5040 , the number of ways is 5040 2 = 2520 . Answer: 2520

Their standing crop biomass at any given time is much less than the biomass of the zooplankton and fishes that feed on them. As we move to higher trophic levels, the biomass increases. 71081.subject: Biology
71081.text: Before industrialization in Great Britain, which insects had a higher population?
71081.sol: Before industrialization in Great Britain, the tree trunks were light-colored due to the abundant growth of white lichens. The white-winged moth, Bistonbetularia , was well camouflaged against these light-colored tree trunks and successfully escaped predation by birds. In contrast, the dark-winged melanic moth, Bistoncarbonaria , was easily spotted against the light background and was heavily preyed upon. As a result, Bistonbetularia had a significantly higher population before industrialization. Answer: Biston bet

71105.subject: Biology
71105.text: It is a natural tendency of organisms to produce more progeny, like, in a span of 750 years, a single pair of male and female elephants would produce ___________ elephants.
71105.sol: According to Charles Darwin's observations on the natural tendency of organisms to overproduce, even the slowest breeding animals can produce an enormous number of offspring over time. Darwin calculated that a single pair of elephants, which are considered among the slowest breeders, would produce approximately 19,000,000 ( 1,90,00,000 ) descendants in a span of 750 years if all of them survived and reproduced. Answer: 1,90,00,000

71495.sol: Statement I is correct as the inner wall of the pollen grain is called the intine, which is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin. The donation of a pair of electrons from the metal into the vacant p orbital of carbon monoxide
The donation of a pair of electrons from a filled p orbital of metal into the vacant orbital of the carbon

121365.subject: Botany
121365.text: What are the examples of partially heterotrophic plants in Kingdom Plantae?
121365.sol: Kingdom Plantae includes all eukaryotic chlorophyll-containing organisms commonly called plants. A few members are partially heterotrophic such as the insectivorous plants or parasites. Bladderwort and Venus fly trap are examples of insectivorous plants and Cuscuta is a parasite. The plant cells have an eukaryotic structure with prominent chloroplasts and cell wall mainly made of cellulose.

121509.subject: Botany
121509.text: Description Kingdom A. Unicellular, eukaryotic organisms 1. Kingdom Monera B. Prokaryotic, non-cellulosic cell wall 2. Kingdom Plantae C. Eukaryotic, multicellular with chitin in cell walls 3. Kingdom Animalia D. Heterotrophic with holozoic nutrition 4. Kingdom Fungi E. Eukaryotic, autotrophic with tissue and organ system 5. Kingdom Protista
121509.sol: A - 5: Unicellular, eukaryotic organisms are placed in Kingdom Protista. Protists are eukaryotes and primarily unicellular, including organisms such as algae and protozoa. B - 1: Prokaryotic organisms with non-cellulosic cell walls are categorized under Kingdom Monera. Monerans include bacteria, which have a cell wall made up of peptidoglycan (not cellulose). C - 4: Eukaryotic, multicellular organisms with chitin in their cell walls belong to Kingdom Fungi. Fungi have chitin in their cell walls and are primarily de

121656.subject: Botany
121656.text: In Whittaker's system of classification, prokaryotes belong to the kingdom
121656.sol: RH Whittaker (1969) proposed a Five Kingdom Classification. The kingdoms defined by him were named-Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia. The main criteria for classification used by him include cell structure, thallus organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. All the prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under kingdom-Monera and unicellular eukaryotic organisms were placed in kingdom Protista. The fungi were placed is a separated kingdom, ie, kingdom-Fungi. The kin

121752.subject: Botany
121752.text: What type of body organization do most red algae have?
121752.sol: The members of rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas. They occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates. The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular . Some of them have complex body organization. The food is stored as floridean starch

121799.subject: Botany
121799.text: From what does the protonema stage develop directly?
121799.sol: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema stage, which develops directly from a spore. It is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage. The second stage is the leafy stage, which develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. They consist of upright, slender axes bearing spirally arranged leaves. They are attached to the soil through multicellular and branched rhizoids. This stage bears the sex orga

122029.subject: Botany
122029.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Gymnosperms produce naked seeds and do not form fruits. Reason (R): In gymnosperms, the ovules are enclosed by an ovary wall before fertilization but become exposed after fertilization. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
122029.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because gymnosperms lack an ovary, which is the anatomical precursor to a fruit. Hence, their seeds are naked and no fruits are formed. Reason (R) is incorrect because in gymnosperms, the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization. They are never enclosed at any stage of their life cycle. Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct

122035.subject: Botany
122035.text: Read the following features regarding a specific pteridophyte: (i) The sporophylls form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones. (ii) It produces two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores. Identify the plant from the given options.
122035.sol: According to NCERT, sporophylls form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones in Selaginella and Equisetum. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores (macro and micro spores) and are known as heterosporous. Equisetum is homosporous, while Salvinia lacks distinct strobili. Pteris is homosporous and lacks strobili. Thus, Selaginella is the only given pteridophyte that possesses both strobili and heterospory. Answer: Selaginella

123974.subject: Botany
123974.text: What is the genetic material of prokaryotic cells surrounded by?
123974.sol: The fluid matrix filling the cell is the cytoplasm . There is no well-defined nucleus. The genetic material is basically naked, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane . In addition to the genomic DNA (the single chromosome/circular DNA), many bacteria have small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA..

124415.subject: Botany
124415.text: Which is incorrect with reference to chloroplast?
options: Occurs only in cells with aerobic respiration
124415.sol: Option (3) is incorrect about chloroplasts. They are spherical, ovoid or disc-shaped cell organelles. These are found in plants and algae. They are involved in photosynthesis due to the presence of chlorophyll in them. During photosynthesis, O ₂ is released. They are not associated with any type of respiration, i.e. aerobic and anaerobic and can be found in any type of cell.

124483.subject: Botany
124483.text: What enables plants to have unlimited growth?
options: Presence of meristems at certain locations in their body
124483.sol: Plant growth is unique because plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life. This ability of the plants is due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body. The cells of such meristems have the capacity to divide and self-perpetuate. The product, however, soon loses the capacity to divide and such cells make up the plant body

124943.subject: Botany
124943.text: What are the end products of glycolysis?
124943.sol: The term glycolysis has originated from the Greek words, glycos for sugar, and lysis for splitting. The scheme of glycolysis was given by Gustav Embden, Otto Meyerhof, and J. Parnas, and is often referred to as the EMP pathway. In anaerobic organisms, it is the only process in respiration. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell and is present in all living organisms. In this process, glucose undergoes partial oxidation to form two molecules of pyruvic acid. In plants, this glucose is derived from sucrose, w

125191.subject: Botany
125191.text: Mitochondria are absent in mature mammalian RBCs. What is the source of energy for these cells then?
125191.sol: Functional mature red blood cells (RBCs) produce energy by fermentation via anaerobic glycolysis of glucose followed by lactic acid production.

125593.subject: Botany
125593.text: Match the historical milestones in the study of photosynthesis in Column-I with the year they were demonstrated or discovered in Column-II. Column-I Column-II (a) Role of air in the growth of green plants (i) 1882 (b) Discovered the release of oxygen (ii) 1854 (c) Evidence for the production of glucose in growing plants (iii) 1770 (d) T.W. Engelmann described the first action spectrum (iv) 1774 Choose the correct ans
125593.sol: The correct chronology is: Joseph Priestley showed the role of air in the growth of green plants in 1770 (a-iii); the release of oxygen in photosynthesis was linked with experiments around 1774 (b-iv); Julius von Sachs provided evidence for glucose production in 1854 (c-ii); and T.W. Engelmann described the first action spectrum of photosynthesis in 1882 (d-i). Hence the correct match is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

125940.subject: Botany
125940.text: What happens to the central cell after triple fusion?
options: It becomes the primary endosperm cell (PEC).
125940.sol: After entering one of the synergids, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the synergid. One of the male gametes moves towards the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus thus completing the syngamy. This results in the formation of a diploid cell, the zygote. 125972.subject: Botany
125972.text: What do the walls of the ovary develop into?
125972.sol: Integuments of ovules harden as tough protective seed coats. As the seed matures, its water content is reduced and seeds become relatively dry (10-15 per cent moisture by mass). The general metabolic activity of the embryo slows down. The embryo may enter a state of inactivity called dormancy, or if favourable conditions are available (adequate moisture, oxygen and suitable temperature), they germinate. As ovules mature into seeds, the ovary develops into a fruit, i.e., the transformation of ovules into seeds and o

126063.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Microsporangium is generally surrounded by four wall layers Reason: The outer two layers perform the function of protection and help in dehiscence of anther to release the pollen

126868.subject: Botany
126868.text: Which one of the following is a fatsoluble vitamin and its related deficiency disease?
126868.sol: Xerophthalmia is a vitamin A (retinol) deficiency disorder which is caused by stoppage of lacrimal activity. Cornea and eye lids become dry and ulcerated. It leads to swelling of dry eye lids and opacity of cornea. Xerophthalmia, if untreated, leads to blindness. Scurvy is vitamin C deficiency disease, Beri beri is vitamin (B₁ ) deficiency disease and Pellagra is caused due to deficiency of niacin.

127167.subject: Botany
127167.text: What is the impact of frequent glaciations in temperate regions on species diversity?
127167.sol: Ecologists and evolutionary biologists have proposed that unlike temperate regions subjected to frequent glaciations in the past, tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years and thus, had a long evolutionary time for species diversification. Frequent glaciations in temperate regions have decreased species diversity .

127311.sol: The number of fungi species in the world is more than the combined total of the species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals."

Occurring at an accelerated rate due to human activities C. Current human impact 3. Lower extinction rates compared to the present D. Pre-human times 4. Responsible for the rapid decline in species numbers
127338.sol: A - 1: The first five mass extinctions were caused by natural events and occurred over millions of years. B - 2: The current sixth extinction is happening at an accelerated rate due to human activities, such as habitat destruction, pollution, and over-exploitation. C - 4: The current human impact is responsible for the rapid decline in species numbers, contributing to the accelerated rates of extinction. D - 3: In pre-human times, extinction rates were much lower than they are today.

127601.subject: Botany
127601.text: What is the detritus food chain made up of?
127601.sol: The detritus food chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter. It is made up of decomposers which are heterotrophic organisms, mainly fungi and bacteria. They meet their energy and nutrient requirements by degrading dead organic matter or detritus. These are also known as saprotrophs (sapro: to decompose). Decomposers secrete digestive enzymes that breakdown dead and waste materials into simple, inorganic materials, which are subsequently absorbed by them.

127602.subject: Botany
127602.text: What do decomposers secrete to break down dead and waste materials?
127602.sol: Decomposers secrete digestive enzymes that breakdown dead and waste materials into simple, inorganic materials. The detritus food chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter. 127838.subject: Botany
127838.text: The bacteria which attack dead animals are
options: first link of the food chain and are known as primary producers
second link of the food chain and are herbivorous
third link of the food chain and are tertiary consumers
the end of food chain and are decomposers.
127838.sol: Bacteria attacking the dead animals represent the end of the food chain and are decomposers. These are the organisms that obtain energy from chemical breakdown of organisms. They secrete enzymes onto dead matter and then absorb the breakdown products. Bacteria are specialised to breakdown organic materials that are difficult for other organisms to digest. They also fulfil a vital role in the ecosystem, returning the constituents of organic matter to the environment in inorganic forms so that they can again be assim

127886.subject: Zoology
127886.text: What are the four types of tissues present in our body?
127886.sol: The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural . We also notice, after some careful study that

128080.subject: Zoology
128080.text: Female Reproductive System Description A. Ovaries 1. Lays 2500-3000 ova B. Oviduct 2. No functional connection C. Connection with Kidneys 3. Arises from ovaries D. Fertilization 4. External, takes place in water
128080.sol: The ovaries can lay 2500-3000 ova, the oviduct arises from the ovaries, there is no functional connection between the ovaries and kidneys, and fertilization is external and takes place in water.

128202.sol: The colourless blood or haemolymph of cockroach has a clear plasma and numerous white corpuscles called haemocytes. Being devoid of any respiratory pigment, it does not serve for gaseous exchange. Its plasma contains about 70 % water. Rest of it is composed of amino acids, uric acid, proteins, sugars, fats, and salts of sodium, potassium, calcium and magnesium. 128698.sol: Wharton's duct is the duct of submandibular salivary gland that opens into the floor of mouth at the junction where front of the tongue meets the mouth's floor.

128928.subject: Zoology
128928.text: What is the route of deoxygenated blood in the body?
options: Venules, veins, and vena cava to right atrium
128928.sol: The blood pumped by the right ventricle enters the pulmonary artery, whereas the left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta. The deoxygenated blood pumped into the pulmonary artery is passed on to the lungs from where the oxygenated blood is carried by the pulmonary veins into the left atrium. This pathway constitutes the pulmonary circulation. The oxygenated blood entering the aorta is carried by a network of arteries, arterioles and capillaries to the tissues from where the deoxygenated blood is collected by a sys

129086.subject: Zoology
129086.sol: Among WBCs, neutrophils, monocytes, eosinophils and basophils are phagocytic cells. But neutrophils and monocytes are primarily phagocytic cells. Eosinophils and basophils can act as phagocytes but this is not their primary function.

129396.subject: Zoology
129396.text: Injury to vagus nerve in humans is not likely to affect
129396.sol: Vagus nerve arises from the side of medulla oblongata. It innervates the larynx, trachea, oesophagus, stomach, lungs, heart and intestines. It is a mixed nerve. It controls the visceral sensations and visceral movements, i.e., heart beat, respiratory movements, peristalsis, sound production, etc. Movement of the tongue is controlled by hypoglossal nerve as it innervates the muscles of the tongue.

130623.subject: Zoology

In this method, popularly known as test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory. 131191.text: Mention the main hormone involved in parturition.
131191.sol: The main hormone involved in parturition is oxytocin.

131210.subject: Zoology
131210.text: How many spermatozoa will be produced from 150 primary spermatocytes?
131210.sol: In spermatogenesis, each primary spermatocyte undergoes the first meiotic division (Meiosis I) to form two secondary spermatocytes. Each secondary spermatocyte then undergoes the second meiotic division (Meiosis II) to form two spermatids. Thus, one primary spermatocyte ultimately yields four haploid spermatids, which differentiate into four spermatozoa. Therefore, 150 primary spermatocytes will produce 150 4 = 600 spermatozoa. Answer: 600

131252.subject: Zoology
131252.text: For normal human fertility, at least 40 per cent of the ejaculated sperms must show vigorous motility. Which specific region of the human sperm and its densely packed constituent organelle directly provide the energy required for this vigorous motility?
131252.sol: According to the criteria for normal human fertility, out of the total ejaculated sperms, at least 60 per cent must have normal shape and size, and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility. The energy required for this vigorous motility is produced by numerous mitochondria. These mitochondria are densely packed specifically in the middle piece of the spermatozoan. 131403.subject: Zoology
131403.text: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA in place of Thymine?
131403.sol: A nucleotide has three components – a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group. There are two types of nitrogenous bases – Purines (Adenine and Guanine), and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine). Cytosine is common for both DNA and RNA and Thymine is present in DNA. Uracil is present in RNA at the place of Thymine. A nitrogenous base is linked to the OH of 1' C pentose sugar through a N-glycosidic linkage to form a nucleoside, such as adenosine

132745.subject: Zoology
132745.text: In which regions did the Neanderthal man live?
132745.sol: The Neanderthal man with a brain size of 1400cc lived in near east and central Asia between 1,00,000-40,000 years back . They used hides to protect their body and buried their dead. Homo sapiens arose in Africa and moved across continents and developed into distinct races. During ice age between 75,000-10,000 years ago modern Homo sapiens arose. Cut the DNA between the base G and A when encounters the DNA sequence 'GAATTC' E. Exonuclease Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
134916.sol: The correct answer is option (4) as EcoRI does not cut the DNA with blunt ends. Instead, it cuts the DNA with sticky / cohesive / staggered ends on each strand. 135453.subject: Zoology
135453.text: Two opposite forces operate in the growth and development of every population. One of them is related to the ability to reproduce at a given rate. The force opposite to it is called
135453.sol: The environmental factors which can check the growth of population size constitute the environmental resistance. These include predators, food, water, nesting sites, similar competitors, etc. All living things tend to reproduce until the point at which their environment becomes a limiting factor. No population, human or otherwise, can grow indefinitely; eventually, some biotic or abiotic variable will begin to limit population growth.

6a0e277c165ae1327797b420.subject: Biology
6a0e277c165ae1327797b420.text: A clown fish lives among the stinging tentacles of a sea anemone and gets protection from predators, while the anemone does not appear to derive any benefit nor is it harmed. This type of ecological interaction is known as:
6a0e277c165ae1327797b420.sol: Commensalism is an ecological interaction between two species in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited (+, 0). The interaction between the sea anemone and the clown fish is a classic example of commensalism. The clown fish gets protection from predators by living among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone, while the sea anemone does not derive any apparent benefit nor is it harmed by hosting the clown fish. Answer: Commensalism

6a252ff098efbb6c17e929a9.sol: The number of moles of solute is calculated by multiplying the concentration by the volume. n = C V n = 0.224 mol L ⁻¹ 3.4 L = 0.7616 mol The concentration 0.224 mol L ⁻¹ has three significant figures, and the volume 3.4 L has two significant figures. In multiplication, the final result must be reported to the least number of significant figures present in the measured quantities, which is two. Rounding 0.7616 mol to two significant figures gives 0.76 mol . Answer: 0.76 mol

95249.subject: Botany
95249.text: Which among the structure has an elongated, unbranched, pointed, and needle-like apices?
95249.sol: Phloem fibers are the dead, unbranched structures with needle-like apices. The cell wall is quite thick, without protoplasm. They are also known as Bast fibers. Phloem fibers of jute, flax, and hemp are used commercially.

95377.subject: Botany
95377.text: Which one of the following groups of three animals each is correctly matched with their one characteristic morphological feature?
options: Animal Morphological features Liver fluke, Sea cucumber Bilateral symmetry
Animal Morphological features Centipede, Prawn, Sea cucumber Jointed appendages
Animal Morphological features Scorpion, Spider, Cockroach Ventral solid central nervous system
Animal Morphological features Cockroach, locust, Taenia Metameric segmentation
95377.sol: Scorpion, spider and cockroach have a ventral solid central nervous system, all belonging to phyla Arthropoda. Bilateral symmetry is found in liver fluke, but sea cucumber has radial symmetry. Metamerism is observed in cockroach and locust (both Arthropoda) but not in Taenia (Platyhelminthes) Joint appendages are a characteristic feature of Arthropoda and sea cucumber is excluded.

95549.subject: Botany
95549.text: Triploblastic, unsegmented, acoelomate exhibit bilateral symmetry reproducing both asexually and sexually, with some parasitic forms. This description is characteristic of the phylum
95549.sol: Triploblastic means having three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. This is seen for the first time in the phylum Platyhelminthes. These are flatworms that exhibit bilateral symmetry. These do not show any body cavity hence are acoelomates. Example: Tapeworms, liver flukes etc. These reproduce by asexual and sexual manner. Thus only this phylum is triploblastic but are acoelomates.

95692.subject: Botany
95692.text: In Beijerinek's experiment, what did he call the infectious fluid that he extracted from diseased tobacco plants?
95692.sol: M.W. Beijerinek (1898) demonstrated that the extract of the infected plants of tobacco could cause infection in healthy plants and called the fluid as Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid). W.M. Stanley (1935) showed that viruses could be crystallised and crystals consist largely of proteins. They are inert outside their specific host cell. Viruses are obligate parasites

95695.subject: Botany
95695.sol: In general, viruses that infect plants have single-stranded RNA. In Tobacco mosaic virus genetic material is single-stranded RNA.

95774.subject: Botany
95774.text: Which of these statements is correct about the five kingdoms given by Whittaker?
options: Most of the kingdoms have organisms with a poorly defined nucleus.
Most of the kingdoms have organisms with a cell wall.
Most of the kingdoms have organisms with only one cell.
Most of the kingdoms have organisms with RNA as the genetic material.
95774.sol: Kingdoms Protista, Plantae, Fungi and Animalia have a well-defined nucleus. Only Kingdom Monera has a poorly defined nucleus. Kingdoms Plantae, Fungi, and Animalia are multicellular. All members of Kingdoms Monera, Protista, Plantae, Fungi, and Animalia have DNA as the genetic material. Kingdoms Monera, Plantae, Fungi have a well defined cell wall.

95863.subject: Botany
95863.text: Match the columns and select the correct option from the following. Column I Column II (A) Wheat rust (I) Edible (B) Antibiotics (II) Puccinia (C) Mushroom (III) Sac fungi (D) Ascomycetes (IV) Penicillium
95863.sol: Wheat rust is caused by Puccinia (Basidiomycetes). Penicillin is an antibiotic obtained from penicillium. Ascomycetes are commonly called Sac fungi as they produce sac-like ascus inside which 4 or 8 ascospores are produced.

96293.subject: Botany
96293.text: During which phase(s) of the cell cycle, the amount of DNA in a cell remains at 4C level if the initial amount is denoted as 2C?
96293.sol: Cell cycle consists of Interphase and Mitotic phase. Interphase is divided into G 1 , S and G 2 stages. Mitotic Phase is the actual division phase and is divided into Karyokinesis and Cytokinesis. DNA is seen in all phases. In M phase both 4C and 2C of DNA is seen. In S phase the synthesis of DNA takes place and hence the amount of DNA doubles. Thus after S phase in G 2 phase the DNA doubles i.e. it becomes 4C.

96434.subject: Botany
96434.text: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Sun is the only source of energy for every single ecosystem on earth.
Ecosystems follow the 2nd law of thermodynamics.
In a terrestrial ecosystem major producers are herbaceous and woody plants.
96434.sol: Sun is not the source of energy in deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem. Ecosystems need energy continuously to synthesize molecules to counteract the tendency of disorderliness. Thus, they follow the second law of thermodynamics. Plants only use 2%–10% of the photosynthetically active radiation which itself is less than 50% of the total incident solar radiation.

96717.subject: Botany
96717.text: Plants deficient in elemental nitrogen, often show its effect on the biosynthesis of:
options: More than one option is correct
96717.sol: Nitrogen is the essential nutrient element required by plants in the greatest amount. It is absorbed mainly as NO 3 – , though some are also taken up as NO 2 – or NH 4 + . Nitrogen is required by all parts of a plant, particularly the meristematic tissues and the metabolically active cells. Nitrogen is one of the major constituents of proteins, nucleic acids, vitamins and hormones.

97074.subject: Botany
97074.text: Plants like Indigofera, Sesbania, lupin and gram:
97074.sol: Indigofera, Sesbania, lupin and gram are members of the Fabaceae family. Members of the Fabaceae family has a zygomorphic flower. They have vexillary aestivation due to which flower can be divided into two equal half from one vertical plane only.

97349.subject: Botany
97349.text: Arithmetic growth rate can be mathematically expressed as:
97349.sol: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures. The simplest expression of arithmetic growth is exemplified by a root elongating at a constant rate. Mathematically, it is expressed as: L t = L 0 + rt L t = length at time ‘t’ L 0 = length at time ‘zero’ r = growth rate / elongation per unit time.

97422.subject: Botany
97422.sol: Equistem belongs to the class of Sphenopsida of phylum Pteridophyta.

97662.subject: Botany
97662.sol: In the TCA cycle, oxaloacetic acid along with water undergoes condensation to form citric acid in the presence of citrate synthase which is then followed by its isomerization into isocitrate. This further undergoes decarboxylation twice to form alpha-ketoglutaric acid and then succinyl-CoA. Succinyl- CoA is then converted to succinic acid and a molecule of GTP is released. This forms the substrate level of phosphorylation.

97734.subject: Botany
97734.text: Which of the following is the site for oxidative decarboxylation?
97734.sol: During complete oxidation of glucose two oxidative decarboxylation reaction occurs one in link reaction when pyruvic acid is oxidized to Acetyl CoA and second in Kreb's cycle when alpha ketoglutaric acid is oxidized to succinyl CoA. Both these reactions occurs in matrix of mitochondria.

97787.subject: Botany
97787.text: In the electron transport system present in the inner mitochondrial membrane, complexes I and IV are respectively ___________.
options: NADH dehydrogenase and F A D H 2
F A D H 2 and NADH dehydrogenase
NADH dehydrogenase and cytochrome oxidase complex
97787.sol: The series of redox reactions taking place between compounds involving electron transfer from donors to acceptors is known as the electron transport chain. In complex I (NADH dehydrogenase) which is the main site of production of superoxide where the NADH loses two electrons which are transferred to ubiquinone. In complex IV (cytochrome oxidase) two molecules of water are produced due to the transfer of electrons from four molecules of cytochrome C to the molecule oxygen.

98032.subject: Chemistry
98032.text: Which one of the following on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride yields a secondary amine ?
98032.sol: Alkyl isocyanides on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride forms secondary amines containing methyl as one of the the alkyl groups.

98157.sol: The C-1 carbon of D (+) glucose is called anomeric carbon or glycosidic carbon and the pairs of stereoisomers differ in configuration around C-1 are called anomers.
